text:
marcos: Quick follow-up on runtime handshake semantics between hosted / dedicated / private. After yesterday's canary we saw two funky cases I want us to agree on: credential handoff and KV cache semantics during rebinds.

zoe: Saw that too. Specifically: 1) hosted->private handoff where hosted issued an ephemeral access token and Private rejected it; 2) dedicated->hosted fallback where we need to decide if we propagate customer creds or use a service principal.

rachel: For compliance, private should never accept hosted-originated long-lived keys. Short-lived delegation tokens might be allowed but only if Private policy permits. We need an explicit "allow_delegate" flag in the manifest.

marcos: Suggest manifest additions: cred_policy (allow_delegate|deny|rebind-required), delegate_ttl, audit_level, and cache_transition (flush|quarantine|merge). Example below.

zoe: Example manifest snippet pls?

rachel: Sure, quick sketch:
```yaml
handshake_v2:
  path: hosted->private
  cred_policy: rebind-required
  delegate_ttl: 60s
  audit_level: full
  cache_transition: quarantine
  fallback_route: service_account
```

tariq: Important: cache_transition needs semantics. quarantine = mark existing entries as tombstoned for new binds, flush = immediate eviction, merge = allow copy-with-versioning. Merge is dangerous for tenant isolation.

marcos: Agreed. We should default quarantine for safety (keeps in-flight safe but prevents reads by new binder). Add cache_version header so we can detect stale reads.

ops-bot: ops-bot: canary "handshake-v2-probe" completed on runtime-canary at 09:45 UTC :eyes:

zoe: Another race: rebind-required means the Private side asks for a rebind before accepting requests. What happens to in-flight requests that used the old binding? We need a transition state machine: ACCEPTING_INFLIGHT -> QUIESCING -> REBINDING -> ACTIVE. Instrument metrics for each.

rachel: Nice. Also need explicit audit events: handshake.request, handshake.accept, handshake.reject(reason), cache.transition(old_version->new_version), creds.issued(source:hosted|service_account). All with tenant_id and correlation_id.

marcos: On fallback_route: service_account is preferred for hosted fallbacks to avoid exposing customer KMS. But service_account path needs policy mapping so observability can attribute cost/latency to the original tenant. Include orig_tenant_id in logs and set restricted scopes on the proxy token.

zoe: One more: eviction semantics on tenant-scoped KV when Private refuses rebind. If Private refuses, should hosted keep the tenant binding sticky or attempt a different region? Suggest add failover_policy: retry-region|retry-hosted|abort.

tariq: implementers note: runtime should expose a small SDK helper that performs the handshake and returns a deterministic state-machine wrapper with callbacks for on_quiesce/on_rebind/on_fail so higher layers can instrument and decide to retry or surface error. Keeps callers simple.

marcos: Action items: 1) update RFC with new manifest fields + defaults (cred_policy: deny, cache_transition: quarantine, fallback_route: service_account, failover_policy: retry-hosted), 2) add state-machine diagram and sample metrics, 3) add an SDK helper prototype in runtime-client. I'll take the RFC update.

rachel: I'll make a short checklist for compliance review + HSM constraints to attach to the RFC.

zoe: I'll prototype the SDK wrapper and wire basic audit events into the canary.

ops-bot: ops-bot: ticket created infra-handshake-254 for SDK wrapper integration :ticket:

marcos: Thanks folks. Let's keep the manifest strict initially and loosen later if we need performance optimizations. :thumbsup:
